lessons.title: Sharing Opinions

items.example: Je pense que c'est une bonne idée.
items.exampleMeaning: I think it's a good idea.

items.example: Je préfère le thé au café.

lessons.tip: In French, the verbs 'aimer', 'détester', 'penser', 'préférer', 'trouver', and 'adorer' are often used to express opinions or feelings. Remember to use the correct subject pronoun with each verb.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Qu'est-ce que tu penses de ce film ?
dialogue.meaning: What do you think of this movie?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: I think it's interesting.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: And the music?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: I love the music!

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Do you like chocolate?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui, j'aime le chocolat, mais je déteste le bruit.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I like chocolate, but I hate noise.

scenario.partnerRole: a friend discussing a movie and music
scenario.brief: Discuss the movie and music you both experienced. Ask questions about opinions.
scenario.goal: You need to express your likes and dislikes.

lessons.title: Discussing Experiences

items.example: J'ai fait un voyage en France.
items.exampleMeaning: I took a trip to France.

items.example: J'ai mangé dans un bon restaurant.
items.exampleMeaning: I ate in a good restaurant.

items.example: J'ai regardé un film hier soir.
items.exampleMeaning: I watched a movie last night.

lessons.tip: The past tense in French is often formed with the auxiliary verbs 'avoir' or 'être'. Remember to match the past participle with the subject when using 'être'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Qu'est-ce que tu as fait le week-end dernier ?
dialogue.meaning: What did you do last weekend?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: I went to the museum.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Et qu'est-ce que tu as vu ?
dialogue.meaning: And what did you see?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: I saw a good movie.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Where did you eat?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: J'ai mangé dans un bon restaurant.
dialogue.meaning: I ate in a good restaurant.

scenario.learnerRole: the person sharing their past activities
scenario.brief: Share what you did last weekend and what you saw or did.
scenario.goal: You need to describe your past experiences.

lessons.title: Likes and Dislikes

items.example: J'aime mieux le thé que le café.
items.exampleMeaning: I like tea better than coffee.

items.example: Je préfère ne pas en parler.
items.exampleMeaning: I prefer not to talk about it.

lessons.tip: When expressing preferences, you can use 'aimer mieux' or 'adorer mieux' to indicate what you like better. Use 'ne pas aimer' to express dislikes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: What kind of movie do you like?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: I like comedies better.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: And this movie, do you like it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Non, je ne l'aime pas. Je le trouve ennuyeux.
dialogue.meaning: No, I don't like it. I find it boring.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tu préfères ne pas en parler ?
dialogue.meaning: Do you prefer not to talk about it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui, je préfère ne pas en parler.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I prefer not to talk about it.

scenario.learnerRole: the person sharing their likes and dislikes
scenario.brief: Discuss your favorite and least favorite movies with your friend.
scenario.goal: You need to express your preferences clearly.

lessons.title: Reflecting on Experiences

items.example: Je me souviens de ce film.
Je veux parler de mes vacances.
items.exampleMeaning: I want to talk about my holidays.

items.example: Nous avons discuté de nos expériences.

items.exampleMeaning: I want to share my memories.

lessons.tip: The verbs 'réfléchir à', 'se souvenir de', 'parler de', 'écrire', 'discuter de', and 'partager' can help you express thoughts about past experiences. Use them to elaborate on your feelings.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: À quoi penses-tu en ce moment ?
dialogue.meaning: What are you thinking about right now?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Je réfléchis à mon voyage en France.
dialogue.meaning: I am reflecting on my trip to France.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tu te souviens de ce film ?
dialogue.meaning: Do you remember this movie?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Oui, je me souviens de ce film.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I remember this movie.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: What do you want to share?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Je veux partager mes souvenirs de vacances.
dialogue.meaning: I want to share my holiday memories.

scenario.partnerRole: a friend reflecting on past experiences
scenario.brief: Discuss your memories and experiences from your travels and holidays.
scenario.goal: You need to reflect and share your thoughts.

scenario.brief: Discuss different topics including movies, music, and travel experiences.
scenario.goal: You need to use vocabulary from the chapter to express your thoughts.
